content:
Requirement R03 (input): Select Autopilot Mode. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to turn the autopilot on..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-03.1, F-03.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-03.<F>.1, Be-03.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-03.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R03 covers activating/engaging the autopilot — turning it ON — via Touch and Keyboard. This is the mode-engagement act, distinct from setting target values (R01) or reading capture status (R02).

**Function candidates:**

**F-03.1 — Engage autopilot control authority.**
Goal: transfer flight control authority from manual to autopilot. The function is the state transition itself (manual → autopilot engaged). Its measurable effect is that the autopilot is now the active controller.

**F-03.2 — Select which autopilot mode is active.**
Goal: not just ON/OFF, but choosing *which* mode (e.g. heading-hold, altitude-hold, nav). The function discriminates among available modes so the correct control law is engaged. Measurable effect: the intended mode is the one that becomes active.

**F-03.3 — Make autopilot availability/armed-vs-engaged state legible for a safe commit.**
Goal: ensure the pilot can only engage when engagement is valid, and knows what will happen on commit. Function is guarding the engagement decision (preventing an unsafe or ambiguous ON). Measurable effect: reduced erroneous engagements.

**My recommendation: F-03.2.** The requirement title is literally "Select Autopilot Mode," and R01 already handles *parameters*. A pure ON/OFF (F-03.1) is too thin and partly overlaps R01/R02. F-03.3 is really a Behaviour concern (validation/feedback) rather than a distinct teleology — it edges into interaction-flow guarding, which belongs below.

Which function do you want to close on?

**F-03.1 — Engage autopilot control authority** is closed.

Goal: transfer flight control authority from manual to autopilot; measurable effect is that the autopilot becomes the active controller.

---

**Behaviour candidates (Touch, Keyboard, Mixed):**

**Be-03.1.1 — Touch-only engage.**
Pilot taps a dedicated autopilot-engage control (AP master) on the WAD. Screen renders the control's state (armed/engaged). Single deliberate tap performs the authority transfer; the widget confirms engaged state visually.

**Be-03.1.2 — Keyboard-only engage.**
Pilot presses a dedicated bezel OSS (or UCP key) mapped to AP-engage. Discrete physical push performs the transfer; screen reflects engaged state. No touch surface needed — usable eyes-out / gloves / vibration.

**Be-03.1.3 — Mixed (either surface, redundant).**
Both the WAD touch control and the bezel OSS are live simultaneously and map to the same engage action; either completes the full task independently. This is what the modality-complete redundancy rule actually requires — not a sequenced hybrid.

**My recommendation:** Be-03.1.3 as the governing behaviour, since the BEHAVIOUR RULE mandates that the pilot can engage using *either* modality alone. Be-03.1.1 and Be-03.1.2 aren't really competing alternatives here — they're the two pathways that Be-03.1.3 unifies.

One flag: the **engage-control surface is shareable** — the same AP-master widget/OSS will also serve R04 (disengage, capability 1.4) and plausibly R01's engagement gating. Worth noting for consolidation, not designing for now.

Which behaviour do you want to close on?

**Be-03.1.3 — Mixed (either surface, redundant engage)** is closed.

Both WAD touch control and bezel OSS are live simultaneously, each mapping to the same engage action; either completes the full task alone.

---

**Structure candidates:**

**S-03.1.3.1 — Dedicated AP-master widget + paired bezel OSS.**
- WAD: a persistent "AP" engage button in a fixed autopilot control panel (on-screen), showing OFF/ARMED/ENGAGED state.
- Bezel: one dedicated OSS adjacent to that panel, hard-mapped to the same engage action, backlit to mirror state.
- Both reflect engaged state via the R02 cue set (green/flashing).
Simple, single-purpose, low-ambiguity. The OSS placement next to the on-screen button gives spatial consistency.

**S-03.1.3.2 — Engage integrated into the autopilot mode panel.**
- WAD: the AP-engage control lives inside the same panel used for R01 target entry — engage sits alongside altitude/heading/speed fields.
- Bezel: a rotary/OSS on that panel's bezel edge doubles as engage (push-to-engage).
- Consolidates all AP interaction in one region.
Fewer separate elements, but couples engage to the parameter panel — risk of accidental engage while entering values.

**S-03.1.3.3 — HOTAS-reachable engage via TDC + on-screen target.**
- WAD: same on-screen AP button as S-03.1.3.1, but sized/placed as a TDC cursor target so the pilot can engage without leaving throttle.
- Bezel OSS retained as the redundant path.
- TDC-select counts as the Touch pathway (cursor-mediated).
Best for hands-on-throttle engagement, but adds a cursor step vs. direct touch.

**My recommendation: S-03.1.3.1.** Cleanest realization of the redundant engage behaviour, keeps engage physically and visually distinct from R01's parameter entry (safety — you don't want engage buried in a value-entry field, per S-03.1.3.2's risk), and reuses the R02 cue set. S-03.1.3.3's TDC benefit is real but is better added as a reuse layer across all engage/commit actions later, not baked in here.

Note: the **bezel OSS and the AP-master widget are shared structure** with the disengage requirement (1.4) — same elements, opposite action.

Which structure do you want to close on?
use uma linguagem mais simples e resumida

**Candidatos de Estrutura:**

**S-03.1.3.1 — Botão "AP" na tela + botão físico no bezel.**
- Na WAD: um botão "AP" fixo que mostra OFF/ARMADO/ENGAJADO.
- No bezel: um OSS dedicado ao lado, com a mesma função, iluminado conforme o estado.
- Ambos usam as cores do R02 (verde/piscando).
Simples e direto.

**S-03.1.3.2 — Engate junto ao painel de parâmetros (R01).**
- O botão de engate fica dentro do mesmo painel onde se digita altitude/rumo/velocidade.
- Um OSS/rotativo do painel também engaja.
Junta tudo num lugar só, mas há risco de engatar sem querer ao digitar valores.

**S-03.1.3.3 — Engate pelo TDC (mão no manete) + botão na tela.**
- Mesmo botão da S-03.1.3.1, mas posicionado para ser alcançado pelo cursor do TDC.
- OSS do bezel continua como caminho redundante.
Bom para não tirar a mão do manete, mas adiciona um passo de cursor.

**Recomendo a S-03.1.3.1.** É a mais limpa, separa o engate da digitação de valores (mais seguro) e reaproveita as cores do R02. O TDC da S-03.1.3.3 é útil, mas melhor tratar depois como camada comum a todas as ações de engate/confirmação.

Obs: o **OSS do bezel e o botão "AP"** são **estrutura compartilhada** com o desengate (1.4) — mesmos elementos, ação oposta.

Qual estrutura você quer fechar?
pode ser a q vc recomendou

**S-03.1.3.1 — Botão "AP" na tela + botão físico no bezel** — fechada.

**Resumo final do R03 (Selecionar/Engajar Modo Autopilot):**
- **Função — F-03.1:** transferir a autoridade de controle do manual para o autopilot.
- **Comportamento — Be-03.1.3:** engate redundante — botão touch da WAD e OSS do bezel ativos ao mesmo tempo; qualquer um completa a tarefa sozinho.
- **Estrutura — S-03.1.3.1:** botão "AP" fixo na WAD (OFF/ARMADO/ENGAJADO) + OSS dedicado no bezel, ambos usando as cores do R02.

**Nota de compartilhamento:** o OSS e o botão "AP" também servirão ao desengate (capacidade 1.4) — mesmos elementos, ação oposta.

R03 completo. Pode fechar o requisito ou seguir para o próximo.
